newsitem.title: USA: Federal Signal expects to meet target in '97.
newsitem.headline: Federal Signal expects to meet target in '97.

text.p: Federal Signal Corp said Wednesday that it expects its 1997 full-year results will meet its long-term earnings objective.
It did not detail that objective. Company officials were not available for comment.
"For the second quarter, our expectations are for good overall results with the Vehicle, Safety and Tool groups taking the lead," Joseph Ross, chairman, said in a statement.
The company said its Sign Group will show an improvement in the second quarter compared with a drop in earnings in the first quarter, but likely will lag the 1996 second quarter.
"Looking at the balance of the year, we expect all four groups to show improvement over the prior year enabling us to achieve our targeted long-term earnings objective this year," Ross said.
Earlier, Federal Signal reported first quarter earnings of $0.30 a share, up from $0.26 a year ago. Sales gained to $224.5 million from $210.8 million.
The company said its Vehicle group's sales rose 13 percent to $125.7 million and its operating income gained 73 percent to $11.7 million.
Safety Products' sales were up eight percent to $49.6 million, but operating income dropped 19 percent to $5.7 million.
Tool sales increased one percent to $34.7 million, but its operating income was off two percent to $7.4 million.
Sign sales fell 25 percent to $14.4 million, and its operating income was off 69 percent to $465,000.
